questions.text: क्लोरोफॉर्म प्रकाश की उपस्थिति में वायु द्वारा ऑक्सीकृत होकर एक विषैली गैस बनाता है जिसे कहते हैं:
questions.text_english: Oxidation of chloroform by air in the presence of sunlight produces a poisonous gas known as:
questions.solution: When chloroform (CHCl3) is oxidised by air (O2) in the presence of sunlight, it produces phosgene gas (COCl2), also known as carbonyl chloride. The reaction is: 2CHCl3 + O2 → 2COCl2 + 2HCl. Phosgene is an extremely poisonous gas that was used as a chemical weapon in World War I. Mustard gas and tear gas are different compounds entirely, and chlorine gas is not the product of this specific oxidation reaction.
questions.solution_hindi: क्लोरोफॉर्म (CHCl3) जब सूर्य के प्रकाश में वायु (O2) द्वारा ऑक्सीकृत होता है, तो फॉस्जीन गैस (COCl2) बनती है। यह अत्यंत विषैली गैस है।

questions.text: लुकास अभिकर्मक निम्न लिखित में से किसके साथ तत्काल धुंधलापन उत्पन्न कर देता है?
questions.text_english: Lucas reagent produces cloudiness immediately with:
questions.solution: Lucas reagent (anhydrous ZnCl2 in concentrated HCl) reacts with alcohols via an SN1 mechanism to produce alkyl chlorides, which are insoluble and appear as cloudiness. Tertiary alcohols react immediately because they form the most stable tertiary carbocations. 2-methyl-2-propanol (tert-butanol) is a tertiary alcohol, so it reacts instantly with Lucas reagent to produce the insoluble tert-butyl chloride, giving immediate cloudiness. Secondary alcohols react within 5 minutes and primary alcohols do not react at room temperature.
questions.solution_hindi: लुकास अभिकर्मक (निर्जल ZnCl2 + सांद्र HCl) तृतीयक ऐल्कोहॉल के साथ तुरंत अभिक्रिया करता है क्योंकि तृतीयक कार्बोकैटायन सबसे स्थायी होता है। 2-मेथिल-2-प्रोपेनॉल एक तृतीयक ऐल्कोहॉल है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से d-कक्षक अष्टफलकीय संकुल में क्षेत्र विपाटन द्वारा अधिक प्रतिकर्षण अनुभव करते हैं?
questions.text_english: Which of the following d-orbitals experience more repulsion in the crystal field splitting of octahedral complex?
questions.solution: In an octahedral crystal field, the six ligands approach along the x, y, and z axes. The d-orbitals that point directly towards the ligands (along the axes) experience greater electrostatic repulsion. The dx²-y² and dz² orbitals point directly along the axes, so they are destabilised and form the eg set with higher energy. The dxy, dyz, and dxz orbitals point between the axes, so they experience less repulsion and form the t2g set with lower energy.
questions.solution_hindi: अष्टफलकीय संकुल में dx²-y² और dz² कक्षक अक्षों के अनुदिश लिगेन्डों की ओर संकेत करते हैं, अतः ये अधिक प्रतिकर्षण अनुभव करते हैं और eg समूह बनाते हैं।

questions.text: लेड विषाक्तता के उपचार के लिए प्रयुक्त कीलेट लिगन्ड है:
questions.text_english: The chelating ligand used for the treatment of lead poisoning is:
questions.solution: EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid) is the chelating ligand used clinically for the treatment of lead poisoning. EDTA is a hexadentate ligand that forms a very stable chelate complex with Pb²⁺ ions, effectively sequestering them from the body tissues. The stable EDTA-Pb complex is then excreted in urine. Dimethylglyoxime is used to detect nickel, en (ethane-1,2-diamine) is a bidentate ligand but not used for lead poisoning, and oxalate is a bidentate ligand used in different contexts.
questions.solution_hindi: EDTA (एथिलीनडाइअमीनटेट्राऐसेटिक अम्ल) एक षट्दंती लिगन्ड है जो Pb²⁺ के साथ स्थायी कीलेट संकुल बनाता है और लेड विषाक्तता के उपचार में प्रयुक्त होता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसकी उपस्थिति के कारण मैंगनेट आयन अनुचुंबकीय होता है?
questions.text_english: Manganate ion is paramagnetic due to the presence of:
questions.solution: Manganate ion is MnO4²⁻, in which manganese is in the +6 oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Mn is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s². In Mn⁶⁺, the configuration becomes [Ar] 3d¹. Therefore, there is one unpaired electron in the 3d orbital, making the manganate ion paramagnetic. A species is paramagnetic when it has one or more unpaired electrons.
questions.solution_hindi: मैंगनेट आयन MnO4²⁻ में Mn की ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था +6 है। Mn⁶⁺ का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास [Ar] 3d¹ है, जिसमें एक अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉन है, इसलिए यह अनुचुंबकीय है।
questions.chapter: The d and f Block Elements
questions.topic: Magnetic properties of transition metal ions

questions.text: C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH और (C2H5)3N के जलीय विलयन में घटती हुई क्षारकता का सही क्रम है:
questions.text_english: The correct order of decreasing basicities of C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH and (C2H5)3N in aqueous solution is:
questions.solution: In aqueous solution, the basicity of aliphatic amines depends on both the inductive effect of alkyl groups (which increases electron density on N) and solvation (hydration of the ammonium ion formed). Diethylamine (C2H5)2NH is the strongest base because it has two ethyl groups providing strong +I effect while still allowing adequate solvation of its conjugate acid. Primary amine C2H5NH2 comes second. Triethylamine (C2H5)3N, despite three ethyl groups, is least basic in aqueous solution because its bulky structure hinders solvation of the protonated form, destabilising the conjugate acid. Hence the order is (C2H5)2NH > C2H5NH2 > (C2H5)3N.
questions.solution_hindi: जलीय विलयन में द्वितीयक ऐमीन (C2H5)2NH सबसे अधिक क्षारीय है क्योंकि +I प्रभाव और जलयोजन के बीच संतुलन अनुकूल है। त्रिएथिलऐमीन में त्रिविम बाधा के कारण जलयोजन कम होती है।
questions.topic: Basicity of aliphatic amines in aqueous solution

questions.text: एक मोलल NaCl विलयन का क्वथनांक, यह मानते हुए कि NaCl जल में पूर्णतः वियोजित हो गया है, है: (जल के लिए Kb = 0·52 K kg mol⁻¹)
questions.text_english: The boiling point of one molal NaCl solution, assuming NaCl to be completely dissociated in water is: (Kb for water = 0·52 K kg mol⁻¹)
questions.solution: NaCl completely dissociates into Na⁺ and Cl⁻, so the van't Hoff factor i = 2. Using the formula ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 2 × 0.52 × 1 = 1.04 K. Therefore, the boiling point of the solution = 100 + 1.04 = 101.04°C. Option A (100.52°C) would be the answer if i = 1 (no dissociation), and options C and D are incorrect values.
questions.solution_hindi: NaCl पूर्णतः वियोजित होकर Na⁺ और Cl⁻ देता है, अतः van't Hoff गुणक i = 2। ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 2 × 0.52 × 1 = 1.04°C। अतः क्वथनांक = 100 + 1.04 = 101.04°C।
questions.topic: Elevation of boiling point and van't Hoff factor

questions.text: जब कोई द्रव और उसके वाष्प साम्यावस्था में हैं तथा दाब को अचानक कम कर दिया जाता है, तो:
questions.text_english: When a liquid and its vapour are at equilibrium and the pressure is suddenly decreased:

options.A: विलयन का वाष्प दाब बढ़ता है

options_english.A: vapour pressure of the solution increases

questions.solution: When pressure is suddenly decreased on a liquid-vapour system at equilibrium, the equilibrium shifts to the side with more moles of gas (i.e., towards the vapour phase) according to Le Chatelier's principle. More liquid evaporates to restore the pressure. Since evaporation is an endothermic process, it absorbs heat from the surroundings, causing the temperature to drop — hence cooling occurs. This is the principle behind refrigeration and why rapidly expanding gases feel cold.
questions.solution_hindi: जब दाब अचानक कम होता है, साम्य वाष्प की ओर स्थानांतरित होता है। वाष्पीकरण एक ऊष्माशोषी प्रक्रिया है, इसलिए आसपास से ऊष्मा अवशोषित होती है और शीतलन होता है।

questions.text:
298 K पर निम्नलिखित सेल पर विचार कीजिए: Mg (s) | Mg²⁺ (1·0 M) || Cu²⁺ (1·0 M) | Cu (s)
उन्हीं पदार्थों का प्रयोग करते हुए हम सेल के विद्युत-वाहक बल (emf) को कैसे बढ़ा सकते हैं?
questions.text_english:
Consider the following cell at 298 K:
Mg (s) | Mg²⁺ (1·0 M) || Cu²⁺ (1·0 M) | Cu (s)
How can we increase the emf of the cell using the same substances?

options.C: [Mg²⁺] और [Cu²⁺] दोनों को 2·0 M तक बढ़ाकर

options_english.A: By decreasing only the [Mg²⁺] to 0·1 M
options_english.B: By decreasing only the [Cu²⁺] to 0·1 M
options_english.C: By increasing both [Mg²⁺] and [Cu²⁺] to 2·0 M
options_english.D: By increasing only the [Mg²⁺] to 2·0 M

questions.solution: By the Nernst equation, Ecell = E°cell - (RT/nF) ln Q, where Q = [Mg²⁺]/[Cu²⁺]. To increase Ecell, we need to decrease Q. Decreasing [Mg²⁺] to 0.1 M while keeping [Cu²⁺] at 1.0 M decreases Q, which decreases the subtracted term and thus increases Ecell. Decreasing [Cu²⁺] would increase Q and decrease emf. Increasing [Mg²⁺] would also increase Q and decrease emf.
questions.solution_hindi: नर्न्स्ट समीकरण के अनुसार, Q = [Mg²⁺]/[Cu²⁺] को घटाने से emf बढ़ता है। केवल [Mg²⁺] को घटाकर 0.1 M करने पर Q घटता है और emf बढ़ता है।

questions.text: किसी प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया का वेग 5·6 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹ है, जब अभिकारक की सांद्रता 0·2 mol L⁻¹ है। वेग स्थिरांक 'k' है:
questions.text_english: The rate of a first order reaction is 5·6 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹, when the concentration of reactant is 0·2 mol L⁻¹. The rate constant 'k' is:
questions.solution: For a first order reaction, Rate = k[A]. Therefore, k = Rate/[A] = (5.6 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹s⁻¹) / (0.2 mol L⁻¹) = 2.8 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. The unit of k for a first order reaction is s⁻¹, which matches option D. Option A gives an incorrect numerical value, and options B and C have incorrect powers of 10.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया के लिए, Rate = k[A]। अतः k = Rate/[A] = (5.6 × 10⁻⁴)/(0.2) = 2.8 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹।
questions.topic: Rate constant calculation for first order reaction

questions.text: न्यूक्लीक अम्ल निम्नलिखित में से किसके बहुलक हैं?
questions.text_english: Nucleic acids are polymers of:
questions.solution: Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are polymers of nucleotides. Each nucleotide consists of three components: a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA), and a phosphate group. Nucleotides are linked together by phosphodiester bonds to form the polynucleotide chain. Amino acids are monomers of proteins, not nucleic acids. Nucleosides lack the phosphate group and cannot polymerise to form nucleic acids on their own.
questions.solution_hindi: न्यूक्लीक अम्ल (DNA और RNA) न्यूक्लियोटाइडों के बहुलक हैं। प्रत्येक न्यूक्लियोटाइड में नाइट्रोजनी क्षार, पेन्टोस शर्करा और फॉस्फेट समूह होते हैं।

questions.text: NaOBr की ऐमाइड के साथ अभिक्रिया में, कार्बोनिल कार्बन निम्नलिखित में से किस रूप में लुप्त होता है?
questions.text_english: In the reaction of NaOBr with amide, the carbonyl carbon is lost as:
questions.solution: The reaction of an amide (RCONH2) with NaOBr is the Hofmann bromamide degradation (Hofmann rearrangement). In alkaline medium (NaOBr = NaOH + Br2), the amide is converted to an amine with one less carbon. The carbonyl carbon is lost as carbonate ion (CO3²⁻) in the alkaline medium, as the reaction proceeds through an isocyanate intermediate (R-N=C=O) which hydrolyses. In strongly alkaline conditions, the CO2 produced reacts with NaOH to form Na2CO3, so the carbonyl carbon is effectively lost as CO3²⁻.
questions.solution_hindi: हॉफमैन ब्रोमएमाइड अपक्रमण (क्षारीय माध्यम में) में कार्बोनिल कार्बन CO3²⁻ के रूप में लुप्त होता है। इस अभिक्रिया में RCONH2 से RNH2 बनता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): ऐल्कोहॉल ब्रन्सटेड क्षारक और ब्रन्सटेड अम्ल दोनों की भाँति कार्य करते हैं।
कारण (R): यह ऑक्सीजन परमाणु पर असहभाजित इलेक्ट्रॉन युगल की उपस्थिति और ध्रुवीय O–H आबंध की उपस्थिति के कारण होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Alcohols act as Bronsted bases as well as Bronsted acids.
Reason (R): It is due to the presence of unshared electron pairs on oxygen atom and presence of polar O–H bond.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. Alcohols act as Bronsted bases because the lone pairs on the oxygen atom can accept a proton (e.g., in reaction with strong acids, R-OH + HCl → R-OH2⁺ + Cl⁻). They act as Bronsted acids because the polar O-H bond allows the hydrogen to be donated as a proton (e.g., R-OH + Na → R-O⁻Na⁺ + ½H2). Both these dual properties are directly caused by the lone pairs on oxygen (enabling base behaviour) and the polar O-H bond (enabling acid behaviour).
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। ऑक्सीजन पर एकाकी इलेक्ट्रॉन युगल क्षारकीय व्यवहार और ध्रुवीय O-H बंध अम्लीय व्यवहार के लिए उत्तरदायी है।
questions.topic: Acidic and basic nature of alcohols

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीनों के डाइऐजोनियम लवणों की तुलना में ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीनों के डाइऐजोनियम लवण अधिक स्थायी होते हैं।
कारण (R): ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीनों के डाइऐजोनियम लवणों में अनुनाद होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Diazonium salts of aromatic amines are more stable than those of aliphatic amines.
Reason (R): Diazonium salts of aliphatic amines undergo resonance.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The assertion is true: aromatic diazonium salts (ArN2⁺) are more stable than aliphatic ones because resonance delocalization of the positive charge over the aromatic ring stabilises them. The reason, however, is false: it is the aromatic diazonium salts (not aliphatic ones) that undergo resonance. Aliphatic diazonium salts are highly unstable because the aliphatic carbocation formed after N2 loss is less stable and there is no resonance stabilisation. So A is correct and R is false — answer is (C).
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन सही है परन्तु कारण गलत है। ऐरोमैटिक डाइऐजोनियम लवण अनुनाद के कारण स्थायी होते हैं, न कि ऐलिफैटिक। ऐलिफैटिक डाइऐजोनियम लवणों में अनुनाद नहीं होता।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): जटिल अभिक्रिया के लिए, अभिक्रिया की कोटि सबसे धीमे चरण द्वारा दी जाती है।
कारण (R): अभिक्रिया की कोटि एक प्रायोगिक मात्रा है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): For complex reaction, order of reaction is given by the slowest step.
Reason (R): Order of a reaction is an experimental quantity.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both statements are true but R does not explain A. The assertion is correct: for a complex (multi-step) reaction, the overall order is determined by the rate-determining (slowest) step, and the order equals the molecularity of that slow step. The reason is also correct: order of reaction is indeed an experimentally determined quantity (it cannot be predicted from stoichiometry alone). However, the reason does not explain why the slowest step determines the order — it is an independent true statement. Hence the answer is (B).
questions.solution_hindi: दोनों कथन सही हैं परन्तु कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता। जटिल अभिक्रिया की कोटि सबसे धीमे चरण से निर्धारित होती है और कोटि एक प्रायोगिक मात्रा है — ये दोनों स्वतंत्र सत्य हैं।
questions.topic: Order of reaction and rate determining step

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): E°(Sc³⁺/Sc²⁺) का मान निम्न होता है।
कारण (R): Sc³⁺ आयन के स्थायित्व के कारण जिसका उत्कृष्ट गैस विन्यास होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): E°(Sc³⁺/Sc²⁺) has low value.
Reason (R): Because of the stability of Sc³⁺ ion which has a noble gas configuration.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. Sc³⁺ has the electronic configuration [Ar] (noble gas configuration), which is exceptionally stable. Because of this high stability of Sc³⁺, reducing it further to Sc²⁺ requires overcoming this extra stability, making the reduction (and thus the E° value) very unfavourable. Hence E°(Sc³⁺/Sc²⁺) is very low (highly negative), meaning Sc³⁺ strongly resists reduction to Sc²⁺.

Example: decomposition of NH3 on platinum surface or decomposition of HI on gold surface

sub_questions.solution: Zero order reactions show rates independent of the concentration of the reactant. sub_questions.text_english: State the condition under which a bimolecular reaction may be kinetically a first order reaction.

key_points: When one reactant is present in large excess (pseudo-first order condition)

sub_questions.solution: A bimolecular reaction becomes kinetically first order (pseudo-first order) when one of the two reactants is present in such a large excess that its concentration remains essentially constant throughout the reaction. For example, in the hydrolysis of an ester (RCOOR' + H2O → products), if water is the solvent and present in great excess, its concentration does not change appreciably, so the reaction appears to depend only on the ester concentration and behaves as first order.

sub_questions.text: हेनरी नियम की सहायता से निम्नलिखित की व्याख्या कीजिए: (i) बेंड्स (Bends) (ii) ऐनॉक्सिया
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the following with the help of Henry's law: (i) Bends (ii) Anoxia

key_points: Bends: at high pressure N2 dissolves in blood; rapid depressurisation causes N2 to bubble out causing pain
Anoxia: at high altitude O2 partial pressure is low so less O2 dissolves in blood

sub_questions.solution: Henry's law states that the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas above the liquid. (i) Bends: Deep-sea divers breathe compressed air at high pressure. At high pressure, more nitrogen dissolves in the blood (Henry's law). If they ascend too rapidly, pressure drops suddenly and nitrogen comes out of solution as bubbles in blood and tissues, causing painful condition called 'bends.' (ii) Anoxia: At high altitudes, the partial pressure of oxygen is low. By Henry's law, less oxygen dissolves in the blood, leading to insufficient oxygen supply to body cells, causing dizziness and weakness — this is anoxia.

sub_questions.text_english: How does sprinkling of salt help in clearing the snow covered roads in hilly areas? Write the name of the colligative property involved in this process.

key_points: Salt lowers the freezing point of water (depression in freezing point)
The colligative property is depression of freezing point

sub_questions.solution: When salt (NaCl) is sprinkled on snow-covered roads, it dissolves in the thin layer of water on the snow surface and forms a solution. According to the colligative property of depression in freezing point, the freezing point of this solution is lower than 0°C. Therefore, the snow/ice melts even at temperatures below 0°C and does not refreeze, helping clear the road. The colligative property involved is depression of freezing point (ΔTf = i × Kf × m).

sub_questions.text_english: Aniline + (CH3CO)2O → A; A + Br2/CH3COOH → B; B + H⁺ → C

key_points: A = Acetanilide (N-phenylacetamide)
B = 4-bromoacetanilide (para-bromo product)
C = 4-bromoaniline

sub_questions.solution: Step 1: Aniline reacts with acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O to undergo acetylation, forming A = acetanilide (PhNHCOCH3). Step 2: Acetanilide undergoes electrophilic bromination with Br2 in acetic acid. The NHCOCH3 group is an ortho/para director. Due to steric factors, the para product predominates, giving B = 4-bromoacetanilide. Step 3: Treatment with H⁺ (acid hydrolysis) removes the acetyl protecting group, giving C = 4-bromoaniline (p-bromoaniline, H2N-C6H4-Br).

key_points: A = 2-methyl-4-bromoaniline (reduction of NO2 to NH2)
B = 2-methyl-4-bromobenzenediazonium chloride (diazotization)
C = 2-bromotoluene (replacement of diazonium by H using H3PO2)

sub_questions.solution: Step 1: The nitro compound (having NO2, CH3, and Br groups on benzene) is reduced with Fe/HCl (Bechamp reduction), converting -NO2 to -NH2. A = 2-methyl-4-bromoaniline. Step 2: Diazotization with NaNO2/HCl at 273-278 K converts -NH2 to -N2⁺Cl⁻. B = 2-methyl-4-bromobenzenediazonium chloride. Step 3: Treatment with H3PO2 (hypophosphorous acid) reduces the diazonium group to H (deamination). C = 2-bromotoluene (1-bromo-2-methylbenzene).

key_points: PhMgBr adds to the CN triple bond to form an imine salt
Hydrolysis gives 1-phenyl-1-propanone (phenyl ethyl ketone / propiophenone)

sub_questions.solution: When propanenitrile (CH3CH2CN) is treated with phenyl magnesium bromide (PhMgBr, a Grignard reagent), the phenyl group adds to the electrophilic carbon of the C≡N bond, forming an intermediate imine salt (after workup). Subsequent acid hydrolysis of this imine gives a ketone. The product is 1-phenylpropan-1-one (propiophenone): C6H5-CO-CH2CH3. key_points: CrO3/(CH3CO)2O oxidises -CH3 to -CH(OAc)2 (acetal of aldehyde)

sub_questions.solution: When p-fluorotoluene (4-F-C6H4-CH3) is treated with CrO3 in the presence of acetic anhydride, the methyl group is oxidised to a geminal diacetate: 4-F-C6H4-CH(OOCCH3)2. This is the Étard-type chromium oxidation in acetic anhydride. On subsequent hydrolysis with aqueous acid, the diacetate is hydrolysed to give p-fluorobenzaldehyde (4-F-C6H4-CHO). This method is specifically used to oxidise a methyl group to an aldehyde without over-oxidation to a carboxylic acid.

sub_questions.text: किसी आयनिक विलयन के प्रतिरोध मापन के लिए दिष्ट धारा (DC) क्यों नहीं प्रयुक्त की जाती है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is direct current (DC) not used to measure the resistance of an ionic solution?

key_points: DC causes electrolysis and changes ionic concentration near electrodes, giving inaccurate readings

sub_questions.solution: Direct current (DC) is not used to measure resistance of ionic solutions because it causes electrolysis. DC causes ions to migrate to and discharge at the electrodes, leading to concentration polarisation near the electrodes. This changes the composition of the solution and produces a back-emf, making the resistance measurement inaccurate. Instead, alternating current (AC) of high frequency is used, as it does not cause permanent migration or discharge of ions.

sub_questions.text: सिल्वर इलेक्ट्रोडों के साथ AgNO3 के जलीय विलयन के विद्युत-अपघटन के उत्पाद, प्लैटिनम इलेक्ट्रोडों के साथ AgNO3 के जलीय विलयन के विद्युत-अपघटन के उत्पादों से भिन्न क्यों होते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are the products of electrolysis different for the electrolysis of aqueous solution of AgNO3 with silver electrodes and electrolysis of aqueous solution of AgNO3 with platinum electrodes?

key_points: With Ag electrodes: active electrodes, anode dissolves (Ag → Ag⁺ + e⁻), cathode deposits Ag
With Pt electrodes: inert electrodes, anode produces O2 (water oxidised), cathode deposits Ag

sub_questions.solution: With silver electrodes (active electrodes), at the anode silver dissolves (Ag → Ag⁺ + e⁻) rather than water being oxidised, while at the cathode Ag⁺ is deposited as Ag. With platinum electrodes (inert electrodes), the anode cannot dissolve; instead water is oxidised to produce O2 gas at the anode. At the cathode, Ag⁺ is deposited as silver in both cases. The key difference is anode behaviour: active Ag anode dissolves, while inert Pt anode evolves O2.

sub_questions.text: जल ले जाने वाली लोहे की पाइपलाइनों में मैग्नीशियम के ब्लॉक क्यों लगा दिए जाते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are magnesium blocks fixed to the iron pipelines carrying water?

key_points: Cathodic (sacrificial) protection: Mg is more electropositive than Fe, so Mg corrodes preferentially, protecting Fe

sub_questions.solution: Magnesium blocks are attached to iron pipelines as a method of cathodic protection (sacrificial anode protection). Magnesium has a more negative reduction potential than iron, meaning it is oxidised more easily. When Mg is connected to the iron pipeline, Mg acts as the anode and corrodes (Mg → Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻), while the iron pipeline acts as the cathode and is protected from corrosion. The magnesium block sacrifices itself to prevent rusting of the iron pipe.

sub_questions.text: जब उपसहसंयोजन यौगिक CoCl3·6NH3 को AgNO3 विलयन के आधिक्य के साथ मिलाया जाता है, तो यौगिक के प्रति मोल के लिए AgCl के 3 मोल अवक्षेपित हो जाते हैं। संकुल का संरचनात्मक सूत्र, IUPAC नाम तथा संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धांत के आधार पर इसका संकरण और चुम्बकीय व्यवहार लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: When a coordination compound CoCl3·6NH3 is mixed with excess of AgNO3 solution, 3 moles of AgCl are precipitated per mole of the compound. Write the structural formula of the complex, IUPAC name, its hybridisation and magnetic behaviour on the basis of valence bond theory.

key_points: Structural formula: [Co(NH3)6]Cl3
IUPAC name: Hexaamminecobalt(III) chloride
Hybridisation: d2sp3 (inner orbital complex)
Magnetic behaviour: diamagnetic (all electrons paired, Co3+ with strong field NH3 ligands)

sub_questions.solution: Since 3 moles of AgCl precipitate per mole of compound, all three Cl⁻ ions are in the outer (ionic) sphere. Therefore, the structural formula is [Co(NH3)6]Cl3. IUPAC name: Hexaamminecobalt(III) chloride. Cobalt is in +3 oxidation state with configuration [Ar] 3d⁶. Since NH3 is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of the 3d electrons. In Co³⁺, 3d⁶ electrons pair in three 3d orbitals, leaving two 3d orbitals empty. These two empty 3d orbitals, along with one 4s and three 4p orbitals, undergo d2sp3 hybridisation to form 6 equivalent hybrid orbitals for the octahedral geometry. Since all electrons are paired (0 unpaired electrons), the complex is diamagnetic.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित प्रत्येक संकुल में कितने ज्यामितीय समावयव सम्भव हैं? (I) [Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻ (II) [Co(NH3)3Cl3]
sub_questions.text_english: How many geometrical isomers are possible in each of the following complexes? (I) [Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻ (II) [Co(NH3)3Cl3]

key_points: (I) [Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻: 0 geometrical isomers (all ligands identical, symmetric)
(II) [Co(NH3)3Cl3]: 2 geometrical isomers (fac and mer)

sub_questions.solution: [Cr(C2O4)3]³⁻ is a tris-bidentate complex of type [M(AA)3]. In an octahedral complex with three identical bidentate ligands, no geometrical isomerism is possible (though optical isomerism exists). Therefore, 0 geometrical isomers. For [Co(NH3)3Cl3], it is of type [MA3B3]. Two geometrical isomers exist: the facial (fac) isomer where the three identical ligands occupy one face of the octahedron, and the meridional (mer) isomer where they lie in a plane. Therefore, 2 geometrical isomers.

sub_questions.text: [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ एक आंतरिक कक्षक संकुल है जबकि [Ni(NH3)6]²⁺ एक बाह्य कक्षक संकुल है। क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ is an inner orbital complex whereas [Ni(NH3)6]²⁺ is an outer orbital complex. Why? [Atomic number: Co=27, Ni=28]

key_points: Co³⁺ (3d⁶) with strong field NH3: electrons pair leaving 2 inner d orbitals free → d2sp3 hybridisation (inner orbital)
Ni²⁺ (3d⁸): 2 electrons remain unpaired even with NH3; inner d orbitals unavailable → sp3d2 hybridisation (outer orbital)

sub_questions.solution: Co has Z=27, so Co³⁺ has configuration [Ar]3d⁶. With strong field NH3 ligands, the 3d⁶ electrons pair up completely, leaving two 3d orbitals empty. These inner (n-1)d orbitals participate in d2sp3 hybridisation, making it an inner orbital complex. Ni has Z=28, so Ni²⁺ has configuration [Ar]3d⁸. Even with NH3, the 3d⁸ electrons cannot fully pair (there are 2 unpaired electrons), leaving no inner 3d orbitals empty for hybridisation. Therefore, the outer 4d orbitals are used in sp3d2 hybridisation, making [Ni(NH3)6]²⁺ an outer orbital complex.

Use: hydrogenation of alkenes (homogeneous catalysis)

sub_questions.solution: Wilkinson's catalyst has the formula RhCl(PPh3)3, i.e., chloridotris(triphenylphosphine)rhodium(I). It is a homogeneous catalyst used for the hydrogenation of alkenes (and alkynes) under mild conditions of temperature and pressure. It selectively hydrogenates non-polar C=C double bonds without affecting other functional groups.

questions.text_english: Calculate the vapour pressure of a solution containing 61 g of benzoic acid (molar mass = 122 g mol⁻¹) dissolved in 500 g of benzene when the vapour pressure of pure benzene at this temperature of experiment is 66 torr. Assume complete dimerization of benzoic acid in benzene.

key_points: Moles of benzoic acid = 61/122 = 0.5 mol
Due to complete dimerization, effective moles of solute = 0.5/2 = 0.25 mol
Moles of benzene (solvent) = 500/78 = 6.41 mol

questions.solution: Moles of benzoic acid = 61/122 = 0.5 mol. Since complete dimerisation occurs in benzene, two molecules of benzoic acid associate to form one dimer. Effective moles of solute particles = 0.5/2 = 0.25 mol. Molar mass of benzene = 78 g mol⁻¹. Moles of benzene = 500/78 = 6.41 mol. Mole fraction of benzene (solvent) = 6.41/(6.41 + 0.25) = 6.41/6.66 = 0.9625. Using Raoult's law: P_solution = P°_benzene × x_benzene = 66 × 0.9625 = 63.52 torr. The vapour pressure of the solution is approximately 63.5 torr.

sub_questions.text_english: Although chlorine shows strong –I effect, yet it is ortho- and para-directing in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions. Why?

key_points: Cl has lone pairs that donate electron density to ring by +M effect (resonance) at ortho/para positions, overriding its –I effect for directing purpose

sub_questions.solution: Chlorine has a strong –I (inductive) effect that withdraws electrons from the ring, making it overall electron-withdrawing and a ring deactivator. However, for directing purposes, chlorine also has a +M (mesomeric/resonance) effect: its lone pairs of electrons on the p-orbital overlap with the π-system and donate electron density back to the ring, specifically to the ortho and para positions. This +M effect dominates the directing influence, making the ortho and para positions relatively electron-rich and more susceptible to electrophilic attack. Hence, Cl deactivates the ring (due to –I) but directs incoming electrophiles to ortho/para positions (due to +M).

Alcohols undergo nucleophilic substitution with hydrogen halides to yield alkyl halides. Dehydration of alcohols gives alkenes. On oxidation, primary alcohols yield aldehydes with mild oxidising agents and carboxylic acids with strong oxidising agents, while secondary alcohols yield ketones. Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation. sub_questions.text_english: Write the mechanism of acid dehydration of ethanol to yield ethene.

key_points: Step 1: Protonation of OH to form oxonium ion
Step 2: Ionisation to form carbocation and water
Step 3: Proton loss to form ethene

sub_questions.solution: The acid dehydration of ethanol to ethene involves three steps. Step 1 (Protonation): The hydroxyl oxygen of ethanol acts as a base and accepts a proton from the acid (H2SO4 or H3PO4) to form an ethyloxonium ion: CH3CH2OH + H⁺ → CH3CH2OH2⁺. Step 2 (Ionisation): The C–O bond breaks heterolytically; water leaves as a leaving group, forming a carbocation: CH3CH2OH2⁺ → CH3CH2⁺ + H2O. Step 3 (Elimination): A base (HSO4⁻ or water) abstracts a proton from the adjacent carbon (β-carbon) of the carbocation, and the electrons form the π bond, yielding ethene: CH3CH2⁺ → CH2=CH2 + H⁺.

sub_questions.text: तृतीयक ऐल्कोहॉल ऑक्सीकरण प्रतिरोधी क्यों होते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are tertiary alcohols resistant to oxidation?

key_points: Tertiary alcohols have no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the OH group, so oxidation (which requires removal of α-H) cannot occur

sub_questions.solution: Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation because the carbon atom bearing the hydroxyl (–OH) group has no hydrogen atom attached to it directly (it is bonded to three carbon groups instead). Oxidation of an alcohol to an aldehyde or ketone requires the removal of a hydrogen from the α-carbon (the carbon bearing –OH). Since no such α-H exists in tertiary alcohols, oxidation under normal conditions does not occur.

sub_questions.solution: In 3-methylphenol, the –OH group directs electrophiles to the ortho (positions 2 and 4 relative to OH) and para positions. With two nitrations, the two NO2 groups enter positions 2 and 4 (ortho and para to OH), giving the major product 2,4-dinitro-3-methylphenol (where OH is at C1, CH3 is at C3, NO2 at C2 and C4).

sub_questions.text_english: Why is ortho-nitrophenol more acidic than ortho-methoxyphenol?

key_points: –NO2 is electron-withdrawing (–I and –M effects) stabilising phenoxide ion
–OCH3 is electron-donating (+M effect) destabilising phenoxide ion

sub_questions.solution: Ortho-nitrophenol is more acidic than ortho-methoxyphenol because the –NO2 group is a strong electron-withdrawing group (by both –I inductive and –M resonance effects). When ortho-nitrophenol loses a proton to form the phenoxide ion, the –NO2 group stabilises the negative charge through resonance and induction, making the phenoxide more stable and thus increasing acidity. In contrast, the –OCH3 group in ortho-methoxyphenol is electron-donating (+M effect), which destabilises the phenoxide ion by increasing negative charge density, thereby reducing acidity.

questions.text_english:
Carbohydrates are optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones or the compounds which produce such units on hydrolysis. They have been broadly classified into three groups — monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides. The carbohydrates may also be classified as either reducing or non-reducing sugars. An important monosaccharide glucose is an aldohexose and is correctly named as D(+)–glucose. It was assigned the open structure on the basis of its reactions with HI, NH2OH, Br2 water, (CH3CO)2O and nitric acid.

Despite having the –CHO group, glucose does not give Schiff's test and hydrogen sulphite addition product with NaHSO3. It was found that glucose forms a six-membered ring in which one of the –OH groups add to the –CHO group and form a cyclic hemiacetal structure.

sub_questions.text: ग्लूकोस में कार्बोनिल समूह की उपस्थिति की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the presence of a carbonyl group in glucose.

key_points: Glucose reacts with NH2OH to form an oxime and with (CH3CO)2O to give a pentaacetate, proving CHO group exists

sub_questions.solution: The presence of a carbonyl (–CHO) group in glucose is shown by its reactions: it reacts with hydroxylamine (NH2OH) to form an oxime (glucose oxime), which is characteristic of aldehydes. It also reacts with acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O to form glucose pentaacetate, indicating five –OH groups and one carbonyl group. Furthermore, glucose can be oxidised by bromine water to gluconic acid (a monocarboxylic acid), confirming the presence of an aldehydic (–CHO) group.

sub_questions.text: ग्लूकोस में पाँच –OH समूहों की उपस्थिति जो भिन्न कार्बन परमाणुओं से जुड़े हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the presence of five –OH groups in glucose which are attached to different carbon atoms.

key_points: Glucose reacts with acetic anhydride to give glucose pentaacetate, proving 5 separate -OH groups on different carbons

sub_questions.solution: The presence of five –OH groups, each on different carbon atoms of glucose, is evidenced by its reaction with acetic anhydride [(CH3CO)2O], which gives glucose pentaacetate. This confirms five free hydroxyl groups, each capable of being acetylated. The fact that reduction with HI and red phosphorus gives n-hexane (a straight-chain 6-carbon compound) confirms that all five OH groups are on different carbon atoms in an unbranched chain.

sub_questions.text: किस प्रकार के कार्बोहाइड्रेटों को अपचायी शर्करा कहते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: What type of carbohydrates are called reducing sugars?

key_points: Carbohydrates that reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagent; those having a free aldehyde or ketone group or those which can open to give such a group

sub_questions.solution: Carbohydrates that reduce Tollens' reagent (AgNO3/NH3) and Fehling's solution (alkaline copper sulphate) are called reducing sugars. These are carbohydrates that have a free aldehyde (–CHO) or ketone (–CO–) group, or those that can open from their cyclic form to generate such a group. All monosaccharides and most disaccharides (like maltose and lactose) are reducing sugars. Sucrose and polysaccharides are non-reducing sugars.

sub_questions.text: D(+)–ग्लूकोस में, अक्षर 'D' और चिह्न '(+)' क्या निरूपित करते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: In D(+)–glucose, what do the letter 'D' and sign '(+)' represent?

key_points: D: configuration of the OH on the penultimate (second-last) carbon is on the right, same as D-glyceraldehyde
(+): dextrorotatory, rotates plane-polarised light to the right

sub_questions.solution: In D(+)–glucose, the letter 'D' refers to the configuration of the molecule. It means that the –OH group on the penultimate (second from the bottom) carbon atom (C5 in glucose) is on the right side in the Fischer projection, analogous to D-glyceraldehyde. This is a relative configuration designation. The sign '(+)' represents the optical rotation: it means the compound is dextrorotatory, i.e., it rotates plane-polarised light to the right (clockwise). Note that 'D' and '(+)' are independent designations; 'D' refers to configuration while '(+)' refers to optical activity.

sub_questions.text: α-D(+)–ग्लूकोस की छः-सदस्यीय वलय संरचना बनाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: Draw the six-membered ring structure of α-D(+)–glucose.

key_points: Haworth projection of α-D-glucopyranose: pyranose ring with OH at C1 (anomeric carbon) on the right/below the ring plane

sub_questions.solution: The six-membered ring structure (Haworth projection) of α-D(+)–glucose (α-D-glucopyranose) is formed when the C5–OH attacks the C1 aldehyde carbon. In the Haworth projection, the ring oxygen is at the back, C1 is on the right. In the α-anomer, the –OH at C1 (anomeric carbon) is on the same side as the ring oxygen in Fischer projection, which translates to being below the ring plane in the Haworth structure. The –CH2OH group at C5 is above the ring. Groups on the right in Fischer projection are below the ring in Haworth projection.

sub_questions.text: MnO क्षारकीय है जबकि Mn2O7 अम्लीय है।
sub_questions.text_english: MnO is basic while Mn2O7 is acidic.

key_points: Lower oxidation state oxides are basic; higher oxidation state oxides are acidic

sub_questions.solution: MnO contains Mn in the +2 (low) oxidation state. In transition metals, lower oxidation states give basic oxides because the metal has a tendency to donate electrons, reacting with acids to form salts. Mn2O7 contains Mn in the +7 (very high) oxidation state. Higher oxidation state oxides are acidic because the highly charged metal centre polarises the O–H bond in water, facilitating proton release. This is a general trend: as oxidation state increases, the oxide character changes from basic to amphoteric to acidic.

sub_questions.text: कॉपर की तुलना में लोहे की उच्चतर कणन एन्थैल्पी होती है।
sub_questions.text_english: Iron has higher enthalpy of atomization than that of copper.

key_points: Fe has more unpaired d-electrons contributing to stronger metallic bonding than Cu which has a filled d-shell and only one 4s electron for bonding

sub_questions.solution: Iron (Fe) has a higher enthalpy of atomization than copper (Cu) because Fe has more unpaired electrons available for metallic bonding. Fe ([Ar]3d⁶4s²) has 4 unpaired 3d electrons plus 2 4s electrons, all of which contribute to the strength of the metallic bond. In contrast, Cu ([Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹) has a completely filled 3d subshell, so only the single 4s electron participates significantly in metallic bonding. Fewer electrons available for bonding means weaker metallic bond and lower enthalpy of atomization for Cu.

sub_questions.text: Cr³⁺ की तुलना में Mn³⁺ एक प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण कर्मक है।
sub_questions.text_english: Mn³⁺ is a stronger oxidising agent than Cr³⁺.

key_points: Mn³⁺ readily gets reduced to Mn²⁺ (half-filled stable d⁵), while Cr³⁺ (half-filled t2g, very stable) resists further reduction

sub_questions.solution: Mn³⁺ is a stronger oxidising agent than Cr³⁺ because Mn³⁺ has a strong tendency to be reduced to Mn²⁺. Mn²⁺ has a 3d⁵ configuration (half-filled d-subshell), which is exceptionally stable due to exchange energy. Therefore, Mn³⁺ readily gains an electron to reach this stable configuration, making it a good oxidising agent. Cr³⁺ (3d³), on the other hand, has a stable half-filled t2g configuration in octahedral complexes and does not readily accept another electron to form Cr²⁺. So Cr³⁺ is a poor oxidising agent compared to Mn³⁺.

sub_questions.text: आप सोडियम क्रोमेट से पोटैशियम डाइक्रोमेट कैसे बनाएँगे? प्रत्येक पद के लिए संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: How do you prepare potassium dichromate from sodium chromate? Write balanced chemical equation for each step.

key_points: Step 1: Na2CrO4 + H2SO4 → Na2Cr2O7 + Na2SO4 + H2O (acidification converts chromate to dichromate)
Step 2: Na2Cr2O7 + 2KCl → K2Cr2O7 + 2NaCl (metathesis on crystallisation)

sub_questions.solution: Potassium dichromate is prepared from sodium chromate in two steps. Step 1: Sodium chromate (Na2CrO4) is treated with dilute sulphuric acid to convert the chromate ion to dichromate ion: 2Na2CrO4 + H2SO4 → Na2Cr2O7 + Na2SO4 + H2O. The yellow chromate ion (CrO4²⁻) is converted to orange dichromate ion (Cr2O7²⁻) in acidic medium. Step 2: The sodium dichromate solution is treated with potassium chloride: Na2Cr2O7 + 2KCl → K2Cr2O7↓ + 2NaCl. Potassium dichromate is less soluble in cold water and crystallises out.

sub_questions.text: लैन्थेनॉयडों की तुलना में ऐक्टिनॉयडों की रसायन अधिक जटिल क्यों होती है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is chemistry of actinoids more complicated as compared to lanthanoids?

key_points: Actinoids show wide range of oxidation states (+2 to +7); 5f, 6d, 7s orbitals are close in energy leading to variable valence; most actinoids are radioactive

sub_questions.solution: The chemistry of actinoids is more complicated than lanthanoids for several reasons. First, in actinoids the 5f, 6d, and 7s orbitals are very close in energy, so electrons can be removed from any of these orbitals, resulting in a wide range of oxidation states (from +2 to +7), unlike lanthanoids which predominantly show +3. Second, 5f orbitals extend further from the nucleus than 4f orbitals, allowing greater participation in bonding. Third, most actinoids are radioactive (especially heavier ones), making their chemistry difficult to study. Finally, the interelectronic repulsion and relativistic effects are more significant in actinoids.

sub_questions.text: प्रथम श्रेणी संक्रमण तत्त्वों (3d श्रेणी) के लिए E°(M²⁺/M) मान नियमित नहीं हैं। क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: E°(M²⁺/M) values are not regular for first row transition elements (3d series). Why?

key_points: E° values depend on sublimation enthalpy, ionisation enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy which vary irregularly across 3d series due to variable electronic configurations

sub_questions.solution: The E°(M²⁺/M) values for first row transition elements are not regular because the electrode potential depends on three energy terms: enthalpy of atomisation (ΔaH), sum of first and second ionisation enthalpies (ΔiH), and enthalpy of hydration of M²⁺ (ΔhydH). Since the electronic configurations of these elements vary irregularly across the series (due to the special stability of half-filled and fully filled d-orbitals), all three of these energy terms change in an irregular manner. The combined effect leads to non-regular E° values across the 3d series.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित की पहचान कीजिए: (I) क्रोमियम का ऑक्सो ऋणायन जो अम्लीय माध्यम में स्थायी है। (II) लैन्थेनॉयड तत्त्व जो +4 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था दर्शाता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify the following: (I) Oxoanion of chromium which is stable in acidic medium. (II) The lanthanoid element that exhibits +4 oxidation state.

key_points: (I) Dichromate ion Cr2O7²⁻
(II) Cerium (Ce)

sub_questions.solution: In acidic medium, the dichromate ion (Cr2O7²⁻) is stable (chromium in +6 state). In basic medium, the chromate ion (CrO4²⁻) is stable. On acidification: 2CrO4²⁻ + 2H⁺ → Cr2O7²⁻ + H2O. So the oxoanion of chromium stable in acidic medium is the dichromate ion (Cr2O7²⁻). Among lanthanoids, cerium (Ce, Z=58) is the element that commonly exhibits the +4 oxidation state, because Ce⁴⁺ has an empty 4f subshell (like xenon configuration), which is extra stable.

sub_questions.text: KMnO4 को गर्म करने पर प्राप्त उत्पादों को लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the products obtained on heating KMnO4.

key_points: 2KMnO4 → K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2 on heating

sub_questions.solution: On heating, potassium permanganate (KMnO4) decomposes as follows: 2KMnO4 → K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2. The products are potassium manganate (K2MnO4, green), manganese dioxide (MnO2, black solid), and oxygen gas (O2). This is a disproportionation reaction where Mn(+7) is reduced to Mn(+4) in MnO2 and converted to Mn(+6) in K2MnO4.

sub_questions.text: प्रागुक्ति कीजिए कि निम्नलिखित आयनों में से कौन-से जलीय विलयन में रंगीन होंगे: Cu⁺, Sc³⁺, Fe²⁺, Ti³⁺, Zn²⁺
sub_questions.text_english: Predict which of the following ions will be coloured in aqueous solution: Cu⁺, Sc³⁺, Fe²⁺, Ti³⁺, Zn²⁺

key_points: Fe²⁺ (d⁶, has unpaired electrons) and Ti³⁺ (d¹, has one electron) will be coloured
Cu⁺ (d¹⁰), Sc³⁺ (d⁰), Zn²⁺ (d¹⁰) will be colourless

sub_questions.solution: Coloured transition metal ions in solution require d-d electronic transitions, which are only possible when there is at least one electron and at least one empty d-orbital in the (n-1)d subshell. Cu⁺ has 3d¹⁰ (completely filled), so no d-d transition is possible — colourless. Sc³⁺ has 3d⁰ (no d electrons) — colourless. Zn²⁺ has 3d¹⁰ (completely filled) — colourless. Fe²⁺ has 3d⁶ (partially filled, 4 unpaired electrons) — coloured (pale green). Ti³⁺ has 3d¹ (one d electron, d-d transition possible) — coloured (purple/violet). So Fe²⁺ and Ti³⁺ will be coloured in aqueous solution.

sub_questions.text: ब्रोमोबेन्जीन से 1-फेनिलएथेनॉल
sub_questions.text_english: Bromobenzene to 1-phenylethanol

key_points: Bromobenzene + Mg/dry ether → PhMgBr; PhMgBr + CH3CHO → adduct; H3O⁺ → 1-phenylethanol

sub_questions.solution: To convert bromobenzene (C6H5Br) to 1-phenylethanol (C6H5CHOHCH3): Step 1 — Treat bromobenzene with magnesium in dry ether to form phenyl magnesium bromide (PhMgBr), the Grignard reagent: C6H5Br + Mg → C6H5MgBr. Step 2 — React PhMgBr with acetaldehyde (CH3CHO, ethanal): C6H5MgBr + CH3CHO → C6H5CH(OMgBr)CH3. Step 3 — Hydrolyse the magnesium alkoxide with dilute acid (H3O⁺): C6H5CH(OMgBr)CH3 + H3O⁺ → C6H5CHOHCH3 (1-phenylethanol).

sub_questions.text: बेन्जीन से m-नाइट्रोऐसीटोफीनोन
sub_questions.text_english: Benzene to m-nitroacetophenone

key_points: Benzene → Friedel-Crafts acylation → acetophenone; acetophenone → nitration (mixed acid) → m-nitroacetophenone

sub_questions.solution: To convert benzene to m-nitroacetophenone: Step 1 — Friedel-Crafts acylation: Benzene reacts with acetic anhydride (or acetyl chloride) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 to give acetophenone (C6H5COCH3). Step 2 — Nitration: Acetophenone is treated with a mixture of conc. HNO3 and conc. H2SO4 (mixed acid). The –COCH3 group is a meta director (electron-withdrawing), so nitration occurs predominantly at the meta position, giving m-nitroacetophenone (3-nitroacetophenone, 3-O2N-C6H4-COCH3).

sub_questions.text: C8H8O आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई कार्बनिक यौगिक 2,4-D.N.P. व्युत्पन्न बनाता है, यह टॉलेन्स अभिकर्मक को अपचित करता है और कैनिजारो अभिक्रिया देता है। यह अम्लीय अथवा क्षारीय KMnO4 के साथ प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण से बेन्जीन-1,2-डाइकार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल देता है। यौगिक को पहचानिए और उत्पादों को लिखिए जब यह कैनिजारो अभिक्रिया देता है।
sub_questions.text_english: An organic compound with the molecular formula C8H8O forms 2,4-DNP derivative, reduces Tollens' reagent and undergoes Cannizzaro reaction. On vigorous oxidation with acidic or alkaline KMnO4 it gives Benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid. Identify the compound and write the products when it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction.

key_points: Compound is 2-methylbenzaldehyde (o-tolualdehyde)
Cannizzaro reaction gives 2-methylbenzyl alcohol and 2-methylbenzoic acid

sub_questions.solution: The compound C8H8O gives 2,4-DNP derivative (carbonyl group present), reduces Tollens' (aldehyde), undergoes Cannizzaro (no α-H, since benzylic CHO), and gives benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid (phthalic acid) on vigorous oxidation — indicating two substituents ortho to each other on benzene. The compound is 2-methylbenzaldehyde (o-tolualdehyde, 2-CH3-C6H4-CHO). In Cannizzaro reaction (with conc. NaOH), two molecules undergo disproportionation: one is oxidised and one is reduced. Products: 2-methylbenzyl alcohol (2-CH3-C6H4-CH2OH) and 2-methylbenzoate ion/2-methylbenzoic acid (2-CH3-C6H4-COO⁻/2-CH3-C6H4-COOH). Equation: 2(2-CH3-C6H4-CHO) + NaOH → 2-CH3-C6H4-CH2OH + 2-CH3-C6H4-COONa.

sub_questions.text:
निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनकी बढ़ती हुई अम्ल प्रबलता के क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
C6H5COOH, O2N–CH2–COOH, CF3–COOH, HCOOH
sub_questions.text_english:
Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their acid strength:
C6H5COOH, O2N–CH2–COOH, CF3–COOH, HCOOH

key_points: C6H5COOH < HCOOH < O2N-CH2-COOH < CF3-COOH

sub_questions.solution: Acid strength increases with better stabilisation of the conjugate base (carboxylate ion), which is enhanced by electron-withdrawing groups. Benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) is the weakest because the phenyl ring donates electrons to the carboxylate through +M effect. Formic acid (HCOOH) is stronger than benzoic acid as there is no electron-donating group. Nitroacetic acid (O2NCH2COOH) is stronger than formic acid because the strong electron-withdrawing –NO2 group (via –I effect) stabilises the carboxylate. Trifluoroacetic acid (CF3COOH) is the strongest because three highly electronegative fluorine atoms exert maximum –I effect, greatly stabilising the carboxylate. Order: C6H5COOH < HCOOH < O2NCH2COOH < CF3COOH.

sub_questions.text: 2,4-डाइनाइट्रोफेनिलहाइड्रेजीन के साथ बेन्जैल्डिहाइड की अभिक्रिया का उत्पाद
sub_questions.text_english: Product when benzaldehyde reacts with 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine

key_points: Benzaldehyde 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone (a yellow/orange precipitate)

sub_questions.solution: When benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) reacts with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP), a condensation reaction occurs at the carbonyl group. The product is benzaldehyde 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone, a yellow to orange crystalline precipitate: C6H5CHO + H2N-NH-C6H3(NO2)2 → C6H5CH=N-NH-C6H3(NO2)2 + H2O. This is used as a test to confirm the presence of a carbonyl group.

sub_questions.text: तनु NaOH की उपस्थिति में ऐसीटोफीनोन के साथ, तत्पश्चात गर्म करने पर
sub_questions.text_english: Acetophenone in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating

key_points: Aldol condensation followed by dehydration to give chalcone (PhCH=CH-CO-Ph, 1,3-diphenyl-2-propen-1-one)

sub_questions.solution: When benzaldehyde reacts with acetophenone in the presence of dilute NaOH, a crossed (mixed) aldol condensation occurs. Benzaldehyde (no α-H) acts as the electrophilic component; acetophenone (with α-H on the methyl group) acts as the nucleophile. In the aldol step, the α-carbon of acetophenone attacks the carbonyl of benzaldehyde, forming a β-hydroxy ketone. On heating, this undergoes dehydration to give chalcone (1,3-diphenyl-2-propen-1-one or benzylideneacetophenone): C6H5CHO + C6H5COCH3 → C6H5CH=CHC6H5CO (chalcone, C6H5CH=CH-CO-C6H5) + H2O.

sub_questions.text: बेन्जोइक अम्ल फ्रीडेल-क्राफ्ट्स अभिक्रिया नहीं देता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Benzoic acid does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction.

key_points: –COOH is electron-withdrawing, deactivates ring; also AlCl3 (Lewis acid) coordinates with COOH group

sub_questions.solution: Benzoic acid does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction for two reasons. First, the –COOH group is a strong electron-withdrawing group (by –I and –M effects) that deactivates the benzene ring towards electrophilic aromatic substitution. Second, the catalyst AlCl3 used in Friedel-Crafts reactions is a Lewis acid that coordinates with the –COOH group to form a stable complex, thereby deactivating the catalyst and preventing the reaction.

sub_questions.text: तुल्य आण्विक द्रव्यमान वाले ऐल्कोहॉलों की तुलना में कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों के क्वथनांक उच्चतर होते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular mass.

key_points: Carboxylic acids form dimers via two O-H...O hydrogen bonds, effectively doubling the molecular mass and requiring more energy to break

sub_questions.solution: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular mass because carboxylic acids form dimeric structures through two intermolecular O–H···O hydrogen bonds between two –COOH groups. This dimerisation effectively doubles the molecular mass and requires significantly more energy to separate the molecules. Alcohols also form hydrogen bonds, but only one O–H per molecule, so their intermolecular attractions are weaker than those of the dimerised acid molecules, resulting in lower boiling points.

sub_questions.text: प्रोपेनैल और प्रोपेनोन में विभेद करने के लिए सरल रासायनिक परीक्षण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write simple chemical test to distinguish between propanal and propanone.

key_points: Tollens' test: propanal gives silver mirror, propanone does not

sub_questions.solution: Propanal (CH3CH2CHO, an aldehyde) and propanone (CH3COCH3, a ketone) can be distinguished by Tollens' test. When treated with Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate, AgNO3/NH3), propanal being an aldehyde gets oxidised and reduces Ag⁺ to metallic silver, forming a shiny silver mirror on the inner walls of the test tube. Propanone, being a ketone, does not reduce Tollens' reagent and no silver mirror is formed.

sub_questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया के लिए E°सेल परिकलित कीजिए जो साम्यावस्था पर है:
Cu (s) + 2Ag⁺ (aq) ⇌ Cu²⁺ (aq) + 2Ag (s)
सेल के लिए साम्य स्थिरांक (Kc) 10¹⁵ है। [दिया गया है: log 10 = 1]
sub_questions.text_english:
Calculate E°cell for the following reaction which is at equilibrium:
Cu (s) + 2Ag⁺ (aq) ⇌ Cu²⁺ (aq) + 2Ag (s)
Equilibrium constant (Kc) for the cell is 10¹⁵. [Given: log 10 = 1]
sub_questions.solution: At equilibrium, the cell EMF = 0. The standard EMF is related to the equilibrium constant by: E°cell = (RT/nF) ln Kc = (0.0591/n) log Kc at 298 K. Here n = 2 (two electrons transferred: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ and 2Ag⁺ + 2e⁻ → 2Ag). Kc = 10¹⁵, so log Kc = 15. E°cell = (0.0591/2) × 15 = 0.02955 × 15 = 0.44325 V ≈ 0.44 V. The standard cell EMF is approximately 0.44 V.

sub_questions.text: लेड संचायक बैटरी के लिए, जब वह उपयोग में होती है, ऐनोड, कैथोड एवं समग्र अभिक्रिया लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write anode, cathode and overall reaction of lead storage battery when it is in use.

key_points: Anode: Pb → PbSO4
Cathode: PbO2 → PbSO4
Overall: Pb + PbO2 + 2H2SO4 → 2PbSO4 + 2H2O

sub_questions.solution: In a lead storage battery during discharge (when in use): Anode (oxidation): Pb(s) + SO4²⁻(aq) → PbSO4(s) + 2e⁻. Cathode (reduction): PbO2(s) + SO4²⁻(aq) + 4H⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l). Overall cell reaction: Pb(s) + PbO2(s) + 2H2SO4(aq) → 2PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l). During discharge, both electrodes form lead sulphate (PbSO4) and sulphuric acid is consumed, reducing the density of the electrolyte.

sub_questions.text: 1 मोल FeO को Fe2O3 में ऑक्सीकृत करने के लिए कितने कूलॉम विद्युत की आवश्यकता होती है?
sub_questions.text_english: How much electricity is required in coulombs for the oxidation of 1 mol of FeO to Fe2O3?

key_points: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻; 1 mol of e⁻ required per mol FeO; Q = 1 × 96500 = 96500 C

sub_questions.solution: In FeO, iron is in +2 oxidation state. In Fe2O3, iron is in +3 oxidation state. The oxidation reaction for 1 mol FeO: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻. One mole of electrons is transferred per mole of Fe²⁺ oxidised. By Faraday's law, the charge required = n × F = 1 × 96500 C = 96500 coulombs. Therefore, 96500 C (approximately 1 Faraday) of electricity is required to oxidise 1 mol of FeO to Fe2O3.

sub_questions.text: 0·0024 M ऐसीटिक अम्ल की चालकता 7·2 × 10⁻⁵ S cm⁻¹ है। यदि ऐसीटिक अम्ल के लिए Λ°m का मान 390·5 S cm² mol⁻¹ है, तो ऐसीटिक अम्ल की वियोजन मात्रा (α) परिकलित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Conductivity of 0·0024 M acetic acid is 7·2 × 10⁻⁵ S cm⁻¹. If Λ°m for acetic acid is 390·5 S cm² mol⁻¹, then calculate the degree of dissociation (α) of acetic acid.
sub_questions.solution: Given: κ = 7.2 × 10⁻⁵ S cm⁻¹, c = 0.0024 M = 0.0024 mol L⁻¹ = 0.0024 × 10⁻³ mol cm⁻³ = 2.4 × 10⁻⁶ mol cm⁻³. Molar conductivity Λm = κ/c = (7.2 × 10⁻⁵ S cm⁻¹)/(2.4 × 10⁻⁶ mol cm⁻³) = 30 S cm² mol⁻¹. Degree of dissociation α = Λm/Λ°m = 30/390.5 = 0.0768 (approximately 7.68%). The degree of dissociation of acetic acid is approximately 0.077 or 7.7%.

sub_questions.text:
25ºC पर निम्नलिखित अर्ध सेल अभिक्रिया के लिए सेल विभव परिकलित कीजिए:
Ag⁺(aq) + 1 e⁻ → Ag (s)
[Ag⁺] = 0·01 M और E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0·80 V [log 10 = 1]
sub_questions.text_english:
Calculate the cell potential for the following half cell reaction at 25ºC:
Ag⁺(aq) + 1 e⁻ → Ag (s)
Given that: [Ag⁺] = 0·01 M and E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0·80 V [log 10 = 1]
sub_questions.solution: Using Nernst equation for the half-cell reaction Ag⁺(aq) + e⁻ → Ag(s): E = E° - (0.0591/n) log (1/[Ag⁺]). Here n = 1, [Ag⁺] = 0.01 M = 10⁻², E° = +0.80 V. E = 0.80 - (0.0591/1) × log(1/0.01) = 0.80 - 0.0591 × log(100) = 0.80 - 0.0591 × 2 = 0.80 - 0.1182 = 0.6818 V ≈ 0.68 V. The cell potential for this half-cell reaction is approximately 0.68 V.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में प्रयुक्त विद्युत-अपघट्य का नाम लिखिए: (I) शुष्क सेल (II) ईंधन सेल (H2–O2)
sub_questions.text_english: Write the name of the electrolyte used in: (I) Dry cell (II) Fuel cell (H2–O2)

key_points: (I) Dry cell: paste of NH4Cl and ZnCl2
(II) H2-O2 fuel cell: concentrated aqueous KOH (potassium hydroxide) solution

sub_questions.solution: In a dry cell (Leclanché cell), the electrolyte is a moist paste of ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) and zinc chloride (ZnCl2). It is called 'dry' because the electrolyte is not in a liquid form. In an H2–O2 fuel cell, the electrolyte used is a concentrated aqueous solution of potassium hydroxide (KOH). The KOH provides the ionic medium through which OH⁻ ions migrate, enabling the electrochemical reactions at both electrodes.
